concepts.name: Sedimentary Basins of India: Classification and Hydrocarbon Potential
key_dimensions: Classification into Category I (proven), Category II (partially explored), and Category III (frontier) basins
Total number of sedimentary basins (~26) vs. basins with proven reserves — a common trap
Which basins are offshore vs. onshore and their relative contribution to production
UPSC trap: Distinguishing 'petroliferous basins' from all sedimentary basins

concepts.name: Mumbai High (Bombay High) Offshore Field: Significance and Decline
key_dimensions: Location in the Arabian Sea — its geographic coordinates and continental shelf context
Historical contribution: Once contributing ~65% of India's crude oil production
Current status: Declining production and ONGC's Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) measures
UPSC trap: Confusing Mumbai High with Mumbai High North and South sub-fields

concepts.name: Krishna-Godavari (KG) Basin: Geology and Strategic Importance
key_dimensions: Straddles both onshore (Andhra Pradesh) and offshore (Bay of Bengal) regions
Reliance Industries' KG-D6 block: Discovery, peak production, and sharp decline controversy
Difference between KG Basin gas fields and KG Basin oil fields
UPSC trap: KG Basin is NOT exclusively offshore — onshore fields also exist near Rajahmundry

concepts.name: Digboi and Assam-Arakan Basin: India's Oldest Oil Region
key_dimensions: Digboi as Asia's oldest oil field (commercial production since 1889) vs. oldest refinery
Assam-Arakan Basin extent: covers Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, and parts of Arunachal Pradesh
Key fields: Digboi, Naharkatiya, Moran, Hugrijan — their relative sizes
UPSC trap: Distinguishing Digboi (Upper Assam) from fields in Brahmaputra Valley broadly

concepts.name: Cambay Basin (Khambhat Basin): Onshore Oil Production
key_dimensions: Location: Gujarat — one of India's most prolific onshore basins
Key fields: Ankleshwar (largest onshore field historically), Kalol, Navagam, Mehsana
Ankleshwar's distinction as India's largest onshore oilfield by historical production
UPSC trap: Cambay Basin is in Gujarat, NOT to be confused with Kutch Basin (also Gujarat but different)

concepts.name: Rajasthan Basin (Barmer Basin): Cairn India and New Discoveries
key_dimensions: Mangala, Bhagyam, and Aishwarya fields — the MBA fields operated by Cairn (now Vedanta)
Mangala field: Largest onshore oil discovery in India in over two decades when found
Rajasthan's transformation from minor to significant oil-producing state after 2009
UPSC trap: Rajasthan oil fields are in Barmer district, not associated with Thar Desert mineral wealth narratives

concepts.name: Offshore vs. Onshore Oil Production: India's Production Geography
key_dimensions: Offshore fields (Mumbai High, KG Basin offshore) contribute the majority of crude production
Onshore fields: Assam, Gujarat (Cambay), Rajasthan
Shift in strategic focus from mature offshore to newer onshore (Rajasthan) and deepwater
UPSC trap: India's largest producer by state — Maharashtra (offshore attributed) vs. Rajasthan (fastest growing)

concepts.name: Natural Gas Fields and Basins: Distinction from Oil Fields
key_dimensions: KG Basin D6 as the most talked-about gas discovery vs. its actual current output
Tripura (Agartala Dome) as a significant natural gas producer — often overlooked
Andhra Pradesh's Ravva field: combined oil and gas significance
UPSC trap: Not all oil fields produce gas and vice versa — KG-D6 was primarily a GAS field, not oil

concepts.name: Kutch Basin and Frontier Basins: Exploratory Potential
key_dimensions: Kutch (Kachchh) Basin: Category II basin with limited proven reserves despite proximity to Gujarat fields
Andaman-Nicobar Basin and Mahanadi Basin as frontier (Category III) basins
Difference between 'in-place resources' and 'recoverable reserves' in frontier basins
UPSC trap: Kutch Basin ≠ Cambay Basin — same state (Gujarat) but geologically distinct

concepts.name: ONGC vs. Private/JV Players: Field Allocation and Production Share
key_dimensions: ONGC dominates production from Mumbai High, Assam fields, and Cambay Basin
Cairn India (Vedanta) operates Rajasthan block under Production Sharing Contract (PSC)
Reliance Industries' KG-D6 block: private sector entry into deep-water gas
UPSC trap: ONGC operates fields both under nomination blocks AND under New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP)

concepts.name: New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) and OALP: Impact on Field Development
key_dimensions: NELP (1999): Replaced nomination regime, introduced competitive bidding for exploration blocks
Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP, 2017): Replaced NELP, allows year-round bidding
Revenue Sharing Contract (RSC) under Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) vs. PSC under NELP
UPSC trap: NELP blocks ≠ all Indian oil fields; legacy fields of ONGC were under nomination, not NELP

concepts.name: Deepwater and Ultra-Deepwater Exploration: India's Frontier
key_dimensions: KG Basin deepwater blocks (D6, D3, D9) — distinction between shallow and deep water fields
Mumbai Offshore Basin deepwater potential beyond Mumbai High
Definition thresholds: Shallow water (<400m), Deepwater (400–1500m), Ultra-deepwater (>1500m)
UPSC trap: India's deepwater focus is primarily in the East Coast (KG, Mahanadi), not West Coast

concepts.name: Coalbed Methane (CBM) and Shale Gas: Non-Conventional Hydrocarbons in India
key_dimensions: CBM blocks in Jharia, Raniganj, Wardha Valley — associated with coal belts, NOT conventional oil basins
Shale gas potential basins: Cambay, KG, Cauvery, Gondwana basins
Difference between CBM policy and shale gas policy in India
UPSC trap: CBM ≠ Coal Gasification; CBM is extracted from coal seams without burning

concepts.name: Cauvery Basin: Southern India's Oil and Gas Potential
key_dimensions: Extends both onshore (Tamil Nadu) and offshore (Bay of Bengal)
Narimanam and Kaveri fields as key producing fields
Relative minor contribution to national production despite significant exploration activity
UPSC trap: Cauvery Basin has both oil AND gas fields — often only gas is remembered

concepts.name: India's Crude Oil Import Dependency and Domestic Production Gap
key_dimensions: India imports ~85% of its crude oil requirement — domestic production meets only ~15%
Top import sources: Iraq, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Russia (post-2022 shift)
Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR) at Padur, Mangaluru, and Visakhapatnam as a buffer
UPSC trap: Domestic production figures vs. refining capacity — India is a net EXPORTER of petroleum PRODUCTS despite importing crude

concepts.name: Natural Gas Pipeline Infrastructure and Field Connectivity
key_dimensions: HVJ (Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur) pipeline: India's longest gas pipeline linking western fields to northern consumers
GSPL and GAIL networks connecting KG Basin gas to southern and northern grids
Agartala (Tripura) gas: connectivity challenges due to landlocked northeastern location
UPSC trap: HVJ pipeline starts from Hazira (Gujarat, near Cambay fields), NOT from Mumbai High

concepts.name: Gas Hydrates: Occurrence and Future Potential in Indian Waters
key_dimensions: India's gas hydrate deposits found in KG Basin and Andaman Sea — among world's largest estimated reserves
NGHP (National Gas Hydrate Programme) expeditions and findings
Difference between gas hydrates and conventional natural gas reservoirs
UPSC trap: Gas hydrates are NOT currently commercially exploited in India — they remain a future resource

concepts.name: Associated vs. Non-Associated Natural Gas: Implications for Production
key_dimensions: Associated gas: produced alongside crude oil (e.g., Mumbai High) — production dependent on oil field status
Non-associated gas: independent gas reservoirs (e.g., KG-D6, Tripura fields)
Flaring of associated gas: India's gas flaring statistics and environmental concerns
UPSC trap: Decline in Mumbai High oil production automatically reduces associated gas output — an indirect consequence often tested

concepts.name: Panna-Mukta-Tapti (PMT) Fields: Joint Venture and Expiry Controversy
key_dimensions: PMT fields in Arabian Sea operated as a JV between ONGC, BG Group (Shell), and Reliance Industries
Contract expiry in 2019 and dispute over field handover and cost recovery
PMT as an example of Production Sharing Contract (PSC) life cycle issues
UPSC trap: PMT fields are OFFSHORE western coast (Arabian Sea), not to be confused with onshore Gujarat fields

concepts.name: Oil Field Terminology: Proven, Probable, and Possible Reserves (3P Classification)
key_dimensions: Proven (1P): 90% probability; Probable (2P): 50%; Possible (3P): 10% — standard SPE definitions
India's proven crude oil reserves figures and their geographic distribution
Difference between 'reserves' (economically recoverable) and 'resources' (total in-place)
UPSC trap: 'India has X billion barrels of reserves' — questions test whether candidates know this refers to PROVEN reserves only
